framework.reasoning: ReAct's main experiments (HotpotQA, FEVER, ALFWorld, WebShop) are pure few-shot in-context prompting against a frozen LLM served over an API (PaLM-540B in the paper; not publicly available). Reproduction therefore centers on an LLM-agnostic prompting/orchestration layer, not a custom neural network -- so no deep-learning framework is strictly required for the core loop. PyTorch is selected as the 'primary' framework only because: (1) the paper's secondary finetuning experiment (Appendix B.1, PaLM-8B/62B decoders trained on 3,000 bootstrapped trajectories) is a standard causal-LM finetuning job, which is most reproducibly implemented via HuggingFace Transformers/PyTorch on an open-weight substitute model; (2) SIR implementation_assumption #1 (confidence 0.95) mandates substituting PaLM-540B with an accessible LLM, and both API-based (GPT-4-class) and open-weight (HF) substitutes should be supported behind a common interface. YAML is used for config (no need for Hydra's multirun/sweep features here). use_huggingface=true covers both the finetuning stage and an optional open-weight inference backend.

tensor_flows.name: ReAct single-step decision (HotpotQA/FEVER, dense-thought)

input.name: c_t
input.shape: variable-length text (few-shot prefix + trajectory so far)

output.name: a_hat_t
output.shape: variable-length text (one Thought or one Action)

steps: TrajectoryContext.to_prompt_string() serializes (o_1,a_1,...,o_{t-1},a_{t-1},o_t) with the loaded few-shot PromptTemplate prefix
LLMClient.generate(prompt, stop_sequences=['\n']) produces raw_text for the next 'Thought i:' or 'Action i:' line
ActionParser.parse(raw_text) classifies raw_text as Thought (if line starts with 'Thought') or DomainAction (search[...]/lookup[...]/finish[...])
if Thought: TrajectoryContext.append_thought(thought) -> context updated, no environment call, loop continues to generate the following Action
if DomainAction: BaseEnvironment.step(action) -> (observation, done, info); TrajectoryContext.append_action_observation(action, observation)
if done (finish[...] called or done=True): ReactAgent.run_episode returns EpisodeResult(trajectory, final_answer=answer, success=..., n_steps=t)
else: loop back to prompt generation for step t+1, subject to max_steps cap (7 for HotpotQA, 5 for FEVER per SIR training_pipeline/backoff heuristic)

tensor_flows.name: ReAct sparse-thought decision loop (ALFWorld/WebShop)

input.name: c_t
input.shape: variable-length text (task description + trajectory so far)

steps: Same generate/parse loop as dense-thought variant, but thought_mode='sparse' relaxes the alternation constraint: the LLM decides for itself whether to emit a Thought before the next Action
BaseEnvironment.step is called only for DomainAction outputs; Thought outputs never reach the environment
Episode terminates when env returns done=True (task success/failure) or max_steps is reached

tensor_flows.name: CoT-SC -> ReAct / ReAct -> CoT-SC routing
steps: ReactCotScRouter.react_then_cotsc: run ReAct up to max_react_steps; if no finish[...] action was produced, fall back to CoTSelfConsistency.sample(n=21, temp=0.7) + majority_vote
ReactCotScRouter.cotsc_then_react: run CoTSelfConsistency.sample(n=21, temp=0.7); compute majority_vote fraction; if fraction < 0.5, fall back to full ReAct episode and use its answer instead

tensor_flows.name: Finetuning forward/backward pass (Appendix B.1 substitute)
steps: TrajectoryFinetuner.build_dataset tokenizes 3,000 ReAct-generated (question/claim, full trajectory) pairs, with prompt tokens masked out of the loss
model(input_ids, labels=masked_labels) -> standard causal LM cross-entropy loss over target trajectory tokens (all thoughts+actions+observations, ASSUMED objective per SIR implementation_assumption)
loss.backward(); optimizer.step() for training_steps as specified per model size / method (4000 for ReAct/Act, 2000-1000 for Standard/CoT depending on model size, batch_size=64)

model.llm_backend: openai  # ASSUMED: PaLM-540B is not publicly accessible (SIR implementation_assumption, confidence 0.95); substitute with GPT-4-class API or HFLocalClient
model.model_name: gpt-4o-mini  # ASSUMED substitute; paper's own substitute ablation used GPT-3 text-davinci-002 (Appendix A.1)

training.optimizer: adamw  # ASSUMED: literature default for PaLM-class finetuning, SIR confidence 0.55
training.learning_rate: null  # NOT SPECIFIED in paper text; ASSUMED, must be swept/tuned, SIR confidence 0.2

hardware.device: cpu  # API-driven agent loop needs no GPU; GPU only required if finetune_enabled=true or HFLocalClient is used
hardware.precision: bf16  # ASSUMED for optional local finetuning runs, SIR confidence 0.2 (not stated in paper)

risk_assessment.description: PaLM-540B, the paper's primary model, is not publicly accessible. Any reproduction necessarily uses a different LLM, so absolute score reproduction (Table 1/3/4 numbers) is not guaranteed even with correct orchestration logic.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implement LLMClient as an abstract interface with OpenAIClient and HFLocalClient backends; report results per-backend and compare relative trends (ReAct > Act, etc.) rather than claiming exact number parity. Mirror the paper's own GPT-3 ablation (Appendix A.1) as a sanity baseline.

risk_assessment.description: Full few-shot exemplar prompts (Appendix C) are not present in the parsed PDF text, only illustrative fragments in Figure 1 and Tables 6-9.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hand-author exemplar trajectories following the documented thought-type taxonomy (decompose goal, extract info, arithmetic/commonsense reasoning, track progress, handle exceptions, reformulate search) and validate qualitatively against the excerpted examples in the paper before large-scale eval runs. Flag PromptTemplate.load() output with a `# TODO: verify against paper Appendix C` marker.

risk_assessment.description: Finetuning stage (Appendix B.1) hyperparameters -- optimizer, learning rate, schedule -- are unspecified in the parsed text.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Default to AdamW with a standard warmup+cosine/linear decay schedule and expose all values via config.yaml with `# ASSUMED` comments; treat train.py's --steps/--batch-size as the only paper-grounded values and everything else as tunable.

risk_assessment.description: WebShop attribute-coverage 'Score' metric's exact normalization formula is not fully specified in the parsed text.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implement MetricsCalculator.webshop_score using the assumed matched/requested ratio, but keep it swappable via config.evaluation and cross-check against the official WebShop repository's scoring function (Yao et al. 2022) before trusting absolute numbers.

risk_assessment.description: ALFWorld and WebShop rely on external simulator packages (alfworld, WebShop repo) with their own installation/data-download requirements (large asset downloads, potential version drift).
risk_assessment.mitigation: Pin alfworld package version, document manual `alfworld-download` data step in README, and implement BaseEnvironment adapters so a missing dependency degrades gracefully (HotpotQA/FEVER experiments remain runnable without ALFWorld/WebShop installed).

risk_assessment.description: Wikipedia API search/lookup fallback behavior (top-5 similar entity suggestion algorithm) is not fully specified.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Use the standard `wikipedia` package's built-in search-suggest and disambiguation handling, which closely mirrors the described fallback behavior; document the substitution in README.

risk_assessment.description: The step cap for the ReAct<->CoT-SC backoff (7 steps HotpotQA, 5 steps FEVER) is explicitly stated, but whether it counts only environment-interacting Actions or also intervening Thoughts is not 100% unambiguous from the text.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implement TrajectoryContext.n_env_steps() to count only DomainAction/Observation pairs (matching 'steps' language used with search/lookup actions in Section 3.2), and expose an alternate total-turn counting mode behind a config flag for sensitivity testing.
